=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5432-5433 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The comment claims "one `gh issue create` per accepted finding, nothing else" but omits the `ensure_label_exists "ai:security"` call that may perform a `gh label create` operation.
  WHY: The comment inaccurately describes API usage and could mislead maintainers about rate-limit sizing; the label operation is cached and this is documentation drift rather than a runtime defect.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5515 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `ensure_label_exists "ai:security"` is called unconditionally for every accepted finding.
  WHY: The helper has an in-process cache, so repeated calls do not generally create labels, but the per-finding invocation is unnecessary and inflates checking overhead.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:security_pass_exhaustion_judge ~lines 5273-5860; security_pass_record_waivers inline | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When a verdict mixes `accept_with_followup`, `keep_fixing`, and `fail` actions, the `failed_count > 0` branch returns before accepted and keep-fixing waivers are processed.
  WHY: Mixed verdicts silently lose partial acceptances and keep-fixing decisions, leaving only terminal failure behavior.
- PR body line 9 — "operator's manual fix #4283" appears twice in the Why section without a `tele-funtoken-msg-scoring/` or other repo prefix. | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The PR body contains the auto-close keyword pattern `fix #4283`, causing the required `lint-pr-body-auto-close` check to fail because the issue lookup cannot prove the body is clean.
  WHY: The PR cannot pass the required lint as written, and squash-merge could auto-close `coding-workflows#4283` if that issue exists; severity was reported as BLOCKER by all reviewers that assigned severity.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:keep_fixing path ~line 5670-5720 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If `create_security_pass_fix_issue` fails, the keep-fixing path can post a verdict comment and then a redundant fail-closed/blocked comment.
  WHY: The second comment may contain stale `round=judge_round` context and confuse operators, although this is not a correctness failure.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:create_security_pass_advisory_followup ~line 5430-5520 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: A failed advisory follow-up issue creation leaves no deduplication record, so later exhaustion rounds retry creation for the same waiver.
  WHY: A transient failure followed by a later success can file duplicate `ai:security` advisory issues because deduplication is populated only after successful creation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:/security-pass-waive handler ~line 15945-16000 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `/security-pass-waive` handler can create real `ai:security` issues when `MOCK_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_JSON` is set because the mock bypasses only the codex call, not GitHub issue creation.
  WHY: A misconfigured test or staging run using a real repository can produce real GitHub side effects because there is no per-finding dry-run or creation gate.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5320-5390 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `security_pass_apply_waivers_to_findings` uses an inline Python script without explicit error handling around file operations.
  WHY: Read failures could cause silent failure or incorrect output.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5390-5420 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `security_pass_record_waivers` uses jq operations without explicit error handling.
  WHY: A corrupted or unwritable `STATE_FILE` could cause the function to fail silently.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5490-5520 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: `create_security_pass_advisory_followup` creates temporary files using printf without guaranteed cleanup.
  WHY: Temporary files could accumulate if the function fails or is interrupted.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: create_security_pass_advisory_followup ~line 5515; comment block ~line 5432 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The comment claims "API cost: one `gh issue create` per accepted finding, nothing else" but ensure_label_exists "ai:security" performs a gh label create call on the first invocation per process.
  WHY: Documentation drift — a future maintainer will believe the per-finding path is a single API call and may treat follow-up issues as free for rate-limit sizing, when in practice the first follow-up also pays a label-create call (cached after that).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: security_pass_exhaustion_judge ~lines 5273-5860; security_pass_record_waivers inline | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When the verdict contains a mix of accept_with_followup, keep_fixing, AND fail actions, the failed_count > 0 branch returns 1 BEFORE the accepted_count loop runs, silently dropping the accepted/keep_fixing waivers.
  WHY: Mixed verdicts lose the partial acceptances. The judge must return an all-or-nothing verdict per call; if it returns a mixed verdict, the only effect is a terminal failure and the operator sees none of the waiver rows that the judge intended to record.
- PR body line 9 — "operator's manual fix #4283" appears twice in the Why section without a `tele-funtoken-msg-scoring/` or other repo prefix. | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The required CI lint job lint-pr-body-auto-close is currently red with: "could not fetch labels for shubhodeep1/coding-workflows#4283 (matched in PR body:line 9)".
  WHY: This PR cannot be merged with the current PR body. Either the script's lookup must succeed or the body must be reworded so `#4283` is qualified or replaced with a non-keyword phrase.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: security_pass_exhaustion_judge keep_fixing path ~line 5670-5720 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the keep_fixing branch's create_security_pass_fix_issue call fails, the function posts a tracking-issue verdict comment and then calls fail_closed, which posts another blocked comment.
  WHY: Two tracking-issue comments fire on the failure path; the second has stale round=judge_round context and may confuse operators.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: create_security_pass_advisory_followup ~line 5430-5520 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When gh_retry gh issue create fails, the waiver row remains recorded without an issue and later exhaustion rounds retry creation.
  WHY: A flaky first attempt can lead to duplicate ai:security advisory issues because deduplication is populated only after successful creation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: /security-pass-waive handler ~line 15945-16000 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The handler runs gh_retry + codex + gh issue create without a per-call or per-finding dry-run gate.
  WHY: A test or staging run with a real repo slug can file real ai:security issues; MOCK_SECURITY_PASS_JUDGE_JSON bypasses codex but not issue creation.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: security_pass_apply_waivers_to_findings 5320-5390 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The inline Python file operations have no error handling.
  WHY: If the findings file or state file cannot be read, the script may fail silently or produce incorrect output.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: security_pass_record_waivers 5390-5420 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The jq operations have no error handling.
  WHY: If STATE_FILE is corrupted or unwritable, the function may fail silently.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: create_security_pass_advisory_followup 5490-5520 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Temporary files are created using printf without guaranteed cleanup.
  WHY: Temporary files could accumulate if the function fails or is interrupted.
- README.md:lines 1470-1476 (12g insertion) and 1530-1541 (env var row) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The "12g. Security-pass exhaustion judge and waivers" paragraph is inserted into an already non-sequential advanced-features block.
  WHY: Readers may miss the feature because the numbering appears disordered, although the numbering scheme is intentionally non-sequential.

=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
